pageCache.text:
Careers Information for Parents
CAREERS INFORMATION FOR PARENTS
Your child’s decisions about their future career choices can become a source of some anxiety for parents. The links below take you to information to help you to support your son /daughter with their future thinking and career planning. Parents can also contact the careers adviser at Trinity School to talk about options/pathways on careerstr@trinitysevenoaks.com
Unifrog is an online platform giving access to information about the range of post-school destinations open to our students including, apprenticeship pathways, employment opportunities, further education options and university courses. It can help students compare every university course, every apprenticeship, and Further Education courses.
www.youthemployment.org.uk/how-to-help-your-child-choose-a-career-careers-advice-for-parents/
GOV.UK – Find an Apprenticeship – is a useful tool to look at apprenticeship opportunities across all levels. https://www.gov.uk/apply-apprenticeship
Not Going To Uni is the #1 website for school and college leavers. Search thousands of jobs, opportunities and apprenticeships in UK and find your perfect fit! Apprenticeships, Distance Learning, Foundation Degrees, Gap Years, Sponsored Degrees, Voluntary Work, Jobs and Training and more can be found here www.notgoingtouni.co.uk/
You can also search for apprenticeship vacancies via Unifrog or through UCAS https://www.ucas.com/apprenticeships
https://amazingapprenticeships.com/parent-zone/ and Amazing Apprenticeships Parents Information
Apply to Uni is designed with the student experience in mind, providing a wide range of up-to-date information on all aspects of applying for a university place, including details about the application process itself, completion of personal statements and an interactive map of university locations as well as containing links to its own library of e-magazines; each one concentrating on a different occupational area. www.applytouni.com/
https://www.ucas.com/undergraduate/what-and-where-study/study-options/how-choose-right-undergraduate-course-you
www.ucas.com/undergraduate/applying-university/ucas-undergraduate-advice-parents-and-guardians
https://www.theuniguide.co.uk/advice/student-finance/how-student-finance-actually-works

pageCache.text:
Trinity Partnership
Trinity School was delighted to officially launch the Trinity Partnership at a special event held in collaboration with the Sevenoaks Chamber of Commerce on Wednesday 4th March.
The event brought together Chamber members, local businesses, and Trinity Partnership members to celebrate the beginning of an exciting initiative aimed at strengthening links between education and industry.
Sixth Form students were also invited to attend, giving them the opportunity to practise their networking skills and speak directly with professionals from a range of sectors. Experiences like this are a key part of helping students develop confidence, build connections and gain insight into future career pathways.
A particular highlight of the evening was hearing from Connie Fenwick (Year 12) and Dax Mantell (Year 13), who volunteered to speak about their time at Trinity and the support they have received from staff when planning their next steps. They spoke about the guidance and resources available to help students explore career pathways, reinforcing the importance of initiatives such as the Trinity Partnership.
The event quickly demonstrated the value of bringing businesses together. One of the partners in attendance arranged a discovery meeting with another local business to explore opportunities for collaboration, while three students were offered work experience opportunities as a direct result of conversations during the morning.
The response to the Trinity Partnership has been extremely encouraging, with many attendees expressing enthusiasm about becoming involved and contributing to the school’s careers programme and wider initiatives.
Over the coming week, a dedicated Trinity Partnership page will be added to the careers section of the Trinity website. This will showcase all current partners involved in the initiative and provide a space where partners can share any offers or benefits available to Trinity staff and parents. For example, Slade Gym are currently offering reduced membership and discounted classes.
The Trinity Partnership is designed to create meaningful connections between students and the world of work, and we look forward to growing this network with the support of our local business community.
We are always keen to hear from local businesses who would like to play a role in inspiring the next generation and supporting Trinity students as they explore future career pathways. Please email astarbuck@trinitysevenoaks.com or careerstr@trinitysevenoaks.com for more information.

pageCache.pageTitle: "Beyond the Rankings: A Parent's Guide to University Applications" by Wendy Heydorn and Julia Barnes. - "Beyond the Rankings: A Parent's Guide to University Applications" by Wendy Heydorn and Julia Barnes. - News - Trinity School
pageCache.text:
News
"Beyond the Rankings: A Parent's Guide to University Applications" by Wendy Heydorn and Julia Barnes.
Over a year ago Julia Barnes and Wendy Heydorn started writing. They had noticed a gap in the resources available for parents seeking to compare post-18 options: UK, US and international university admissions, alongside UK Degree Apprenticeships — so they set out to fill it.
Between them they bring over 25 years of Higher Education guidance experience — Wendy spent sixteen years advising students at Sevenoaks School and has co-authored three IB text books with Cambridge University Press and last year Laurence Goodwin and she co-authored “An Educator’s Guide to University Applications" with Trotman. Julia has over a decade of Higher Education guidance experience at Sevenoaks School, US admissions expertise as an accredited Times Higher Education Counsellor, and the perspective of a parent of four — three of whom have recently been through university applications themselves. She is also a parent at Trinity and has been a governor here for the last four years.
They thought that a book for parents, guardians and carers was needed. The higher education landscape has changed so much since they were 18: Degree Apprenticeships, the rise of the student commuter, the increasing level of competition for the most competitive courses, changes to admissions tests, the reformed Personal Statement. Not only is the landscape shifting, graduate employment is getting tougher and the impact of AI raises yet more questions about the future of work. Then there's the child in front of a parent; their own teenager with their own strengths, talents, and potential.
Understandably, parents often turn to university rankings. But league tables tell them nothing about whether a course or a campus is right for their child. Where is a parent to begin making sense of this? This book helps parents begin and continue a conversation with their children about what comes next. Universities in the UK and US already have brilliant parent-facing resources and the book draws on these, with expert contributions from across the sector. It offers a comparative approach to different pathways: UK, US and international universities, and Degree Apprenticeships, and suggest how parents can support their son or daughter in Years 11, 12 or 13. This is for the families who understandably wonder where to begin.
Available at Amazon.co.uk : beyond the rankings

pageCache.pageTitle: SEND: Frequently Asked Questions - Trinity School
pageCache.text:
SEND: Frequently Asked Questions
* Trinity School recognises that there is mixed medical and scientific consensus about the existence of syndromes or conditions relating to “visual stress” and that research findings vary in terms of the measurable benefits of the use of coloured overlays, coloured paper or filtered lenses to those who experience difficulties with reading.
However, in line with our ethos to support our students to reach their full academic potential and make a successful transition to adulthood, we believe we should acknowledge the symptoms of such a condition and try to provide students with support and resources related to it.
There are many different options when it comes to getting help with visual stress. The diagnostic assessment/treatment of visual stress and other visual processing difficulties takes place within a commercial, profit-led market and as such providers of these services dictate their own charges. Our staff are not qualified to diagnose medical, ophthalmological or mental health conditions and we understand parents may wish to seek assistance from trained professionals.
* My child had extra time (access arrangements) and assessments printed on coloured paper at Primary, do they get this throughout their schooling and GCSE exams?
The evidence collected by the end of Year 9, will help us identify those student’s that require further investigation and testing from our official Access Arrangements assessor at the start of KS4. You will be notified if your son/ daughter has been identified at this stage. It is also important to note that a diagnosis report will be used as evidence to back up the KS3 investigation, although they cannot solely be used to support an application without evidence from teachers.
This process also applies to KS5 (sixth form) mainly for new students to this centre.

pageCache.text:
What Parents' Say About us
"I wanted to take a moment to write and express my sincere gratitude for the fantastic experience my son had on his first day in Year 8 at Trinity yesterday. He came home absolutely buzzing, and as a parent, it has been incredibly reassuring to see him so energised and excited about his education.
Thank you to you and your staff for creating such a nurturing, intellectually stimulating, and welcoming culture. We are so glad to be part of the Trinity community and are very much looking forward to the year ahead." (Year 8 Parent - September 2026)
"…she has thoroughly enjoyed her time at Trinity and has greatly appreciated the support, care and encouragement she has received…
We would like to take this opportunity to sincerely thank all of the staff for the education, guidance and support they have provided during X time at the school. She has had a very positive experience and has benefited enormously from the opportunities, encouragement and friendships she has gained during her time at Trinity." (Parent - September 2026)
"I Just wanted to email to say how delighted we were with X's A level results! and to acknowledge our thanks to the Trinity team for the support and teaching that X has received during his time at Trinity. Trinity has been a wonderful place for him to spend his secondary school education and the most important part to us is that he has been very happy there and made some wonderful friends.
Thanks again to you and all the wonderful staff" (Year 13 Parent - July 2026)
"I just wanted to send a heartfelt thank you to everyone involved in organising yesterday's Transition Day.
Everything was so well organised and it created such a welcoming atmosphere for both the children and their parents.
From the moment we arrived, everyone was so kind and helpful. As a parent, I couldn't have wished for a better outcome.
What touched me most was seeing Trinity's Christian values of kindness, care and belonging lived out throughout the day." (Parent of new Year 7)
"We are so pleased with everything at Trinity, all the amazing teachers and everything they do for X." (Parent - June 2026)
"I felt compelled to write to you to express my sincere appreciation to everyone at Trinity School. He came to you in Year 7 at a 'just about on target' child and he left with fantastic GCSE and A Level results which enabled him to get a place at his University of choice.
Now I am so pleased to say yesterday he obtained a BA 1st Class Honours for his Degree. This is AMAZING and I truly believe it is down to the fantastic pathway that Trinity put him on." (Parent - June 2026)
"I would just like to say a massive thank to your amazing and wonderful staff for looking after X.
I have always had nothing but praise for Trinity School." (Parent - June 2026)
"I truly believe that Trinity has been incredible, particularly in Year 11, with many members of your staff going above & beyond 'their job'." (Parent - June 2026)
"What came across to us was how caring and community spirited the school is, while also recognising that academics are important. It's refreshing that Trinity recognises how important it is to deal with the whole child, and we feel lucky that X is at the best school for him." (Grandparent - June 2026)
"It was an absolute delight to visit Trinity School. I was very impressed with all I saw and heard on my visit". (Grandparent - June 2026)
"He is doing very well he's now a chef. I am still very sure his time at Trinity, although very short, changed him. His confidence and socialisation skills improved massively."
I am so so thankful for his time at your school." (Parent of a former pupil - May 2026)
"The Trinity Sixth Form has been transformational for X, after doing well in her GCSEs this new-found confidence propelled her to step out of her comfort zone.
We are so deeply grateful for the transformational education that Trinity provides for life in all its fullness. It is a unique place, as I know visitors often remark, you can feel the difference in the atmosphere of sincere love and genuine community." (Parent - May 2026)
"The academic, social, and emotional support you have provided has made her learning journey not only smoother, but truly enjoyable. More schools should follow this model!" (Parent - May 2026)
"Working at Trinity School will always be one of the highlights of my time working in schools. It has such a supportive and caring community, and it has been wonderful to be part of it." (Staff member - May 2026)
“I just wanted to say a big thank you for all your hard work in putting together the Frozen Jr. production. We saw it last night and thought it was fantastic, the whole cast were so professional and polished, while also clearly enjoying themselves! I really appreciate how much effort goes into a production like that, so thank you to you and the whole team for all the hours of planning and rehearsals you put in, it definitely paid off!" (Parent - April 2026)
“I just wanted to say what an amazing performance the kids put on yesterday, thank you to you and all the staff that make these shows happen, I shed a few tears of joy because they were all just brilliant." (Parent - April 2026)
"Thank you also for the continued support for X – it’s very reassuring to know she feels happy and supported at Trinity." (Parent - April 2026)
"I love working at Trinity, there is a great team spirit and a lot of respect for each other as teachers, as well as genuine care for the pupils." (Teacher - April 2026)
"Ever since she’s joined Trinity, she’s become a brand-new girl! Seeing her hard work recognised and rewarded is a great boost and has given her the confidence to dream big (like, very big - she’s talking Cambridge!). This is such a huge credit to you and the rest of the staff." (Parent - March 2026)
"What an event! What a School! And the Chaplaincy stuff is not too bad either!" (Visitor - February 2026)
"A massive thank you to you and all of your fantastic staff. In our opinion Trinity School is exceptional in its love, care and education. From years 7 to 13 our sons have been supported, cared for and encouraged everyday of their school journey.
It hasn’t always been easy but even in the toughest of times you and your staff have gone above and beyond to do everything possible to encourage and support them, helping them to develop into the caring, compassionate and academically successful students they have become." (Parent - December 2025)
"A big thank you in general to yourself and all the teachers & staff at Trinity. We know how hard you all work to make it such a great school and we appreciate all that you do." (Parent - December 2025)
"I just wanted to say a big thank you to you all for taking the students to the OCC packing centre today. My son came home and said "it was the best school trip I've ever been on!". I am so grateful to the school for showing him how much fun it can be serving others and helping those less fortunate than himself. It will have been such a valuable experience." (Parent - December 2025)
"Can I just say thank you for hosting this. It just makes me glad and appreciate that my son is a student at Trinity." (Parent - November 2025)
"Honestly, this was brilliant. The interactive exercises to demonstrate what you were talking about worked really well. I thought you pitched the level just right, too. I felt lucky to have my child in a school that would commit time, energy and resources to creating sessions like this for parents. Thank you!"
(Parent - November 2025)
"I just wanted to tell you what a fantastic job you did last night at your 6th form open evening. I was especially impressed with the students we spoke to re BTEC sport and History.
We were also impressed with the teachers we met, Maths especially for bringing a tough and sometimes dry subject to life, Geography and Economics. A real passion shining through and teaching is a tough job! Top marks Trinity." (Parent - November 2025)
"I’m just so thrilled with how much he enjoyed the experience, and it’s really confirmed for me that Trinity was the right choice for my son, the support he’s receiving means so much." (Year 7 Parent - October 2025)
"I just want to thank you for the Parent Survey response circulated last week. I took a minute to read it now and it is just fantastic!
Again, you and your staff are doing a BRILLIANT JOB and we are so appreciative of the thoughts that go into every day, the planning and input in our children's lives." (Parent - October 2025)
"I just feel that I need to write to say how amazing Mr Bashford is! He is my daughter's form tutor. Mr Bashford goes above and beyond for all the children, the support and encouragement is second to none. He is an absolute asset to the school!!" (Parent - September 2025)
"I just wanted to take a moment to say how incredibly impressed I am with Trinity. X has enjoyed her first couple of weeks tremendously, and I love hearing all about it. The teachers have been firm but compassionate, and the staff attentive and supportive – from helping her find her classroom, to smiling and interacting with her in the car park, it’s these little touches that really help her to feel at home.
In particular, I’d like to commend the librarians, who have created a safe and peaceful environment where students can relax while deepening their love for books. The Growing Hope extracurricular club has been another highlight.
I can honestly say that Trinity has a special ‘spark’ that seems to set it apart.
I simply wanted to express my gratitude and let you know how much I appreciate the work you all do." (Parent - September 2025)
"As parents, we've been impressed with the levels of integrity and excellence displayed at Trinity School and know we made the correct choice sending our son and his older brother to your establishment." (Parent - July 2025)
"They don’t realise how lucky they are sometimes and this was a good reminder that the leadership/staff do care." (Parent - June 2025)
"There is a supportive ethos that has been developed within the school itself that values the qualities he requires of himself every day" (Grandparent - June 2025)

Trinity LifeBites (PSHE & RSE)
Trinity LifeBites (PSHE & RSE)
"Personal development is a strength of the school and is well supported through the ‘Trinity LifeBites’ programme, covering personal, social and health education as well as relationships and sex education. The programme is exceptionally well designed to offer pupils a wide, rich set of experiences in a coherently planned way. The programme also covers careers which are carefully mapped out and actively supported through careers fairs, visiting speakers and external visits. The programme (Lifebites) is exceptionally well designed to offer pupils a wide, rich set of experiences in a coherently planned way."
At Trinity School, our PSHE (personal, social, health and economic) and RSE (relationship and sex education) programmes are called Trinity LifeBites.
The intent of our LifeBites programme is to equip young people to develop skills to fulfil their God-given potential. It helps them through critical thinking to develop informed, considered decisions and strategies as they navigate their way now and along the complex, dynamic road towards adulthood. This includes learning how to be resilient and knowing where to get support when needed.
This part of our curriculum is sensitive to our Christian ethos. It is designed as a spiral, building on learning in primary school and then throughout their time at Trinity from Year 7 to Year 13. This allows us to build and expand on ideas at appropriate times in their education. The LifeBites programme fosters students’ critical thinking and leadership skills, including the ability to respectfully discuss, debate, and pose thoughtful questions about complex topics across subjects.
Healthy relationships, mental and physical wellbeing are at the core of this. We ensure that we cover the DfE’s statutory guidelines, financial education and leadership. In addition, we include career guidance to support the career programme, allowing us to meet the Gatsby benchmarks.
The programme from Year 7-Year 13 is divided into broad topic areas including:
Trinity LifeBites is delivered during form time each week, and across the curriculum where subject departments focus on areas relevant to their specialisms during the course of the year. For example, in computing students will learn about online safety, in science they will learn about puberty and the reproductive organs, while in history students will discuss anti-Semitism. In addition, the Heads of Key Stage and SLT also reiterate relevant areas during assemblies, such as media literacy and safeguarding. Our staff are trained and supported to deliver this aspect of the curriculum to fulfil our mission: ‘Education for life in all its fullness’.
LifeBites provides students with the opportunity to explore Christian perspectives on the topics and issues they are studying. At every stage, students are encouraged to think critically, ask questions, and come to their own conclusions.
Christian teachings considered in LifeBites include:
As a school, we focus on healthy relationships every day, addressing issues such as sexism, bullying, racism, misogyny, homophobia, and stereotyping. These issues are specifically addressed in LifeBites but equally addressed through a broader school culture that does not tolerate them, and any occurrences are promptly identified and addressed. Our pastoral approach and behaviour expectations make this clear.
Please find below details of our programme which are also in each student’s planner. The programme may need to be amended from time to time. Each year we tackle new topics reflective of societal issues and changing statutory guidance, while circling back and building on key concepts such as internet safety, healthy relationships and mental wellbeing.
If you have any questions, please do not hesitate to contact the Assistant Headteacher, Personal Development, Mrs D Gale: dgale@trinitysevenoaks.com

Careers Programme & Policies
If you are a parent, local employer or business owner and would like to get involved in supporting the careers programme at Trinity School we would love to hear from you - please contact Lois Tinkler (Careers Leader) at ltinkler@trinitysevenoaks.com to talk about future opportunities.
Students at Trinity School are encouraged to explore a wide range of career choices through our Education, Information, Advice and Guidance programme (CEIAG), which has been designed to fulfil the Gatsby Benchmarks as follows:
We are committed to the continuous development of our CEIAG programme and we measure and evaluate the impact of our careers programme by using The Careers and Enterprise Company's Compass tool. We also seek feedback from students following careers activities using form group discussion and online forms, which is used to inform and improve the delivery of future careers sessions.
We are building links with local employers through support from the Careers and Enterprise Company. We are a member of the West Kent Careers Education Information & Advice Group (CEIAG) and the West Kent Enterprise Advisors Network.
The Trinity School – Careers Programme
All Trinity students have access to the Unifrog careers platform, where students can:
At Key Stage 3, students are involved in understanding the different career paths available through exploring a range of job sectors, learning about career routes linked to subject areas, challenging workplace stereotypes, investigating qualifications and making appropriate choices for GCSE.
Careers Weeks take place 3 times throughout the year where subject teachers introduce students to jobs/careers that their individual subjects could lead on to. Assemblies and a parent and pupil information evening on choosing options are also provided.
All students will have had meaningful encounters with providers of apprenticeships and technical education opportunities through year group assemblies.
At Key Stage 4, pupils continue research into careers and pathways post-16 inc. the Sixth Form, FE provision, apprenticeships, and higher education. They develop skills in CV and application form writing, develop their own career plan, and understand the qualifications framework beyond GCSE.
All students will have had meaningful encounters with providers of apprenticeships and technical education opportunities through year group assemblies and the post-16 external provider event.
Careers Weeks take place 3 times throughout the year where subject teachers introduce students to jobs/careers that their individual subjects could lead on to.
In Year 10 students will complete a work experience placement supported by the school together with specialist work experience provider Changing Education. They will also attend an assembly about the full range of post-16 opportunities available inc. 6th form, FE provision, T-levels and apprenticeships.
In Year 11 students will attend talks by the sixth form and North Kent College about the course options they offer, sign up to KentChoices to make post-16 applications and have the option to attend specific workshop sessions to support apprenticeship/employment applications. Students will have access to careers guidance via 1-2-1s &/or small group sessions
At Key Stage 5, students continue to explore careers and pathways post-18 inc. University and employment/apprenticeship routes and develop their own career plan.
Students have access to a series of careers lectures delivered by universities and employers through the Friday Talks calendar. Some of these lectures, together with form time, are devoted to the topic of UCAS applications and interview skills. There are also UCAS evenings, student finance evenings and apprenticeship information events.
All students can access impartial 1-2-1 careers guidance support in Year 12 and 13.
In Year 12 students have a week of self-arranged work experience, where they develop skills in writing prospective applications and developing initial employer relationships. Students also take part in a mock interview day.
In Year 13 all students are offered support to complete their UCAS personal statement. For those applying to university they are also supported to complete their application and prepare for interviews. For those students choosing employment or apprenticeship options they are offered support in finding suitable vacancies and to prepare for interview.

News
Year 10 Silver Training Expedition, Ashdown Forest, 26th-28th March
37 Year 10 students spent three days navigating various parts of the Ashdown Forest. Students had to plan their routes, carry their own equipment and working together as they navigated unfamiliar terrain. At camp they were responsible for putting up tents, preparing and cooking their own meals and keeping the site clean and tidy. Students were tired, cold, wet and found the weekend challenging yet rewarding. By the end of the expedition, all students felt proud of what they had achieved and more confident in their ability to cope with challenges, making the experience both memorable and meaningful.
The DofE team are very proud of all students that took part for their enthusiasm, resilience and exemplary behaviour.

Key Stage 5: Years 12 & 13
Key Stage 5 (Years 12 and 13)
At Post-16, students choose from a wide range of Advanced Level and Level 3 BTEC courses, can study the AQA Extended Project Qualification. Trinity’s offer of traditional A levels alongside Level 3 BTEC qualifications offers both a flexible yet challenging curriculum which enables our learners to access high quality higher education and employment after Sixth form.
Nationally, A Levels remain the most widely recognised British Level 3 qualification; combined with the career-based knowledge and required in BTEC Extended Certificates students have an enviable range of level 3 study options, which ensure there is no limit to the university courses and employment routes that Trinity students can access.
At Trinity, our study programmes are all designed to be full-time with a minimum of 540 planned hours per academic year. The school offers 19 A level courses, as well as Tech Level L3 courses in Digital Media, and Sports and Applied General L3 courses in Health and Social Care and ICT. Students may follow up to four courses in both year 12 and year 13. In Year 12, all students follow a core programme including PSHE, PE and supervised study. Trinity students are also expected to complete a Level 3 Extended Project alongside service activities which count towards the awarding of the Trinity diploma.
